entities.summary:
Frederick of La Roche was the sixth Latin archbishop of Tyre (1164–1174) and chancellor of the kingdom of Jerusalem, playing a crucial role in King Amalric's diplomatic efforts. Born into the Lorrainer family of counts of La Roche, he rose to prominence through his education and administrative skills. His significance in the medieval period lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Christian kingdoms of the Holy Land.

As a key figure in the kingdom of Jerusalem, Frederick of La Roche oversaw the construction of several important infrastructure projects, including the expansion of the city's walls and the development of its harbor. He also played a key role in the kingdom's military campaigns, participating in several battles against the Muslim forces of the Ayyubid dynasty.

Frederick of La Roche's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Latin Church in the region, as well as the ongoing rivalries between the Christian kingdoms of the Holy Land. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure a fragile peace between the kingdoms, which would eventually give way to the devastating conflicts of the 13th century.

One of the most striking aspects of Frederick of La Roche's time as archbishop of Tyre was the presence of a group of Templar knights who arrived in the city in the late 12th century. The Templars would go on to play a significant role in the kingdom's military campaigns and would become a major force in the region for centuries to come.

The region of Tyre, with its strategic location on the Mediterranean, was a critical hub of trade and commerce in the medieval period. The city's harbor was an important center for the shipment of goods, including spices, textiles, and other luxury items. The expansion of the city's walls and the development of its harbor were crucial projects that helped to establish Tyre as a major power in the region.
